answers.question: Do all your drones use the same charging connector?
answers.expect: no — several connector types are in use, and they are not interchangeable (3.b1)
answers.answer: We have several drone models from different manufacturers, and they use several connector types that are not interchangeable. Each company has its own charging pads at its own sites, a few dozen of them. I keep drones and charging equipment in working order, and pads are never lent to another company.

answers.question: Who sets up the charging pads at your company's sites?
answers.expect: the fleet technicians (2.b1)
answers.answer: I add new drones to the fleet, retire old ones, set up charging pads at my company's sites, and take drones out of service for repairs and put them back. I also send drones to charge and keep them and the charging equipment in working order.

answers.question: Does anyone watch every drone all the time?
answers.expect: no — nobody watches every drone at every moment; one person may be responsible for hundreds (6.b5)
answers.answer: Nobody watches every drone at every moment, and one person may be responsible for hundreds. Drones fly on their own autopilots while people on the ground supervise.

answers.question: Do the companies want the service to guarantee that they meet the regulations?
answers.expect: no — they want no guarantee of meeting regulations and no compliance audit (8.b4)
answers.answer: I don't know.

answers.question: What can go wrong with the links you use to instruct the charging equipment?
answers.expect: they are unreliable; an instruction may get through twice, and the sender often cannot tell whether the first attempt arrived (6.b6)
answers.answer: The links used to give instructions to the charging equipment are unreliable, meaning an instruction may get through twice. Furthermore, the sender often cannot tell whether the first attempt arrived.

answers.question: Do your drones ever restart while they are flying?
answers.expect: yes — sometimes, after a software fault, and they carry on (6.b3)
answers.answer: Yes, drones sometimes restart in flight after a software fault and carry on. Batteries also drain faster in cold and wind than planned, and radios have patchy coverage around industrial sites, ports, and in bad weather.

answers.answer: I don't know.

answers.answer: No, the companies do not want several languages.
